title: Interleaved Capacity Heuristics and Delegated Scope Voting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We frequently face mid-cycle pressure where multiple initiatives request surge capacity and product leads struggle to decide which scope to cut. Current approaches (top-down triage or ad-hoc negotiation) are slow and opaque, causing missed deadlines and morale friction.

Goal: Define a lightweight, operationalizable heuristic and small democratic mechanism for delegated scope-cuts and tranche scheduling so teams can 1) make defensible mid-cycle capacity decisions within 48 hours, 2) minimize coordination overhead, and 3) preserve alignment with OKRs.

Proposal summary: 1) Establish a tranche scheduler heuristic that ranks incoming surge requests by a composite score (OKR alignment, customer urgency, unblocked work ratio, infra cost delta). 2) Form a rotating 5-person Cycle Crew (PM, Eng Tech Lead, Product Designer, Infra SRE rep, Customer Success rep) empowered to approve tranche adjustments up to N engineer-weeks per repo. 3) Introduce delegated scope voting for non-blocking scope cuts: when a team proposes a cut, stakeholders cast ranked-choice votes from a bounded list of candidate cuts; the Cycle Crew executes the top-ranked cut unless vetoed by an explicit emergency policy. 4) Bake simple guardrails (max per-team cut percent, auto-rollback window, and mandatory post-tranche retrospective).

Why this is different: blends deterministic heuristics for triage with a light delegation of decision power and a small democratic voting flow for non-emergency cuts. Prior playbooks emphasize manual reserves or canary surges; this is designed to scale across 10+ concurrent initiatives while maintaining transparency and traceability.
acceptance_criteria: A documented tranche scoring formula with weights and examples
A cadence and roster for the Cycle Crew defined and published
A voting template and one simulated run recorded with results
Integration points specified: Reporter -> Cycle Crew Slack channel, updated capacity sheet, and Console runway dashboard signal
One pilot across 3 teams completed and retrospective written
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Agreed to use a composite score (OKR alignment 35%, customer urgency 30%, unblocked work 20%, infra cost delta 15%). 2025-02-15: Leadership approved a 5-person rotating Cycle Crew and delegated authority up to 2 engineer-weeks per repo for mid-cycle tranche adjustments. 2025-02-18: Decided to pilot with three volunteer squads in March; veto is limited to security or compliance-impacting cuts only.
tasks: Draft tranche scoring rubric and worked examples (owner: PM)
Define Cycle Crew charter, rotation cadence, and on-call calendar (owner: Ops)
Build a minimal Google Form / Slack workflow for delegated scope voting (owner: PD/Eng)
Add capacity signal flags to Console runway dashboard (owner: Eng Infra)
Run end-to-end pilot with 3 squads and capture telemetry + qualitative feedback (owner: PM)
Write final playbook and publish to Confluence (owner: PM)
Post-pilot retro and decision to adopt/iterate (owner: PM)
